_comment: Every asset the manifest cannot derive, declared with its digest. This file is the
INPUT; prov.asset_manifest merges it into server/data/assets.json, and that one file
is what the build, the fetch and the verify all read. Regenerate with
python -m prov.asset_manifest --repo . --out server/data/assets.json
Two kinds of entry, and the difference is where the bytes are canonical.
The build-host inputs ('provenance' absent) were never in git at all: their canonical
copies live in the content store on mast-ns-control, each carrying a PROVENANCE.md
written from this file by tools/write-vendor-provenance.py. 'prefix' is where such an
input is keyed in the one asset namespace -- the path its files would have if they
were tracked -- so the machine-wide cache mirrors the repo tree.
The 'git-lfs' entry ('provenance': false) is different: those 162 files ARE still in
this repository, and their digests were derived from the LFS pointers until #48 froze
them here. A derived digest stops being derivable the moment the pointer goes, so the
freeze happens BEFORE the untracking rather than with it -- and while both exist,
test_asset_manifest.py checks every frozen digest against the pointer it came from.
It spans every module and the client media, so it declares explicit paths and no prefix.
'cached' says whether an entry is fetched into C:\MAST\provider-assets at all -- the
NoMachine seats are issued certificates and deliberately are not, which is what
Assert-MastNoNoMachineCertsInAssets enforces.
'kind' is the shape the entry has in the canonical store, which is not always its shape
in the cache: the PlateSolve3 installer and its data payload are one directory there and
two files beside the planewave certs here. write-vendor-provenance.py keys on it -- a
'file' entry must not get a directory of its own, which is how full-frame.fits was
replaced by one.
C:\MAST\ on the build host also holds regenerable images and scratch; those are in
'not_vendor_inputs' with the reason, so the distinction is recorded rather than
remembered. Kept in step with the build by server/prov/tests/test_vendor_inputs.py.

inputs.name: mast-indexes
inputs.why_not_in_repo: 9.9 GB of astrometry.net index FITS; far past what git-LFS should carry, and 71% of every payload.
inputs.origin: Extracted once from the legacy 15 GB index image by build/extract-index-seed.ps1. Upstream is astrometry.net index series 5202+5203.
inputs.reacquire: build/extract-index-seed.ps1, against the legacy .img, or re-download the series from astrometry.net.

inputs.name: full-frame.fits
inputs.why_not_in_repo: 90 MB of real sky data; the solve input the astrometry smoke test needs to be a real solve rather than a skipped one.
inputs.origin: A mast00 full frame. The astrometry verify's solve arguments are tuned to this specific frame.
inputs.reacquire: Any comparable MAST full frame, but verify-astrometry.ps1's solve parameters would need re-tuning.

inputs.name: ps3-catalog
inputs.why_not_in_repo: 2.0 GB PlaneWave vendor download (Setup_PlateSolve3_Catalog.exe plus its Inno data payload .bin). Both must stay together and keep their exact names.
inputs.origin: Downloaded from planewave.com. Real UCAC4/Orca catalog for PlateSolve3.
inputs.reacquire: Re-download from planewave.com; without it 'ps3cli --server' has no catalog and the planewave verify fails.

inputs.name: cygwin-pkg-cache
inputs.why_not_in_repo: A frozen harvest of a working unit's own cygwin package cache, not a redistributable artifact.
inputs.origin: Harvested from a provisioned unit by build/harvest-cygwin-cache.ps1. Deliberately frozen: the itefix mirror is rolling, and moving past cygwin 3.6.9 broke the pinned fitsio wheel (#20).
inputs.reacquire: build/harvest-cygwin-cache.ps1 against a unit still on the pinned cygwin version. Re-harvesting from a newer mirror is NOT equivalent.

inputs.name: nomachine-licenses
inputs.why_not_in_repo: Issued license certificates. Secrets: gitignored, one seat per unit, tracked in server/providers/nomachine/assets/licenses/allocated.csv.
inputs.origin: Issued by NoMachine and originally held on mast-ns-control.
inputs.reacquire: Re-issue through NoMachine; a lost seat is a purchase, not a download. Relative to the repo top, not under C:\MAST\.

inputs.name: git-lfs
inputs.why_not_in_repo: Vendored binaries that git-LFS carried until MAST_provisioning#48 retired it. Frozen here because a digest derived from a pointer stops being derivable the moment the pointer is removed, and the index must not quietly lose 162 rows.
inputs.origin: Tracked in this repository via git-LFS. These digests are the ones the pointers recorded, frozen here when #48 retired LFS; until the untracking the pointers are still in the tree and each is checked against its row.
inputs.reacquire: The blobstore on mast-ns-control holds every one of these digests. While the pointers remain, git lfs pull also restores them.

not_vendor_inputs.reason: Superseded. The legacy index image the mast-indexes seed was extracted from once; the unit now builds its own sparse image from the seed. Kept only as the input to a re-extraction, and not worth 15 GB of mirror.
